content:
Facts: The son of a surviving spouse sought reduction of a holographic will that granted the spouse a life usufruct over all assets and appointed a niece as heir, alleging infringement of the spouse’s reserved share and claiming monetary reinstatement.
Legal framework
Articles 540, 554, 557, 564 and 649 of the Italian Civil Code on reserved shares, reduction, succession of the legitimate heir and rights of habitation and use; principles on interpretation of testamentary dispositions and valuation of estates.
Interpretative issue
Whether a testamentary attribution of general usufruct constitutes an institution of heir and whether co-heirs appointed by the same will are exempt from acceptance with benefit of inventory; how monetary reinstatement of the reserved share must be calculated.
Principle applied
A testamentary disposition granting a general usufruct over all assets qualifies as an institution of heir rather than a legacy, absent contrary indications. Where both claimant and defendant are co-heirs appointed by the same will, acceptance with benefit of inventory under Article 564 ICC is not required. Testamentary dispositions exceeding the disposable portion are subject to reduction within statutory limits. The value of the estate and the infringement of the reserved share must be assessed at the opening of the succession through fictitious reconstitution; when reinstatement occurs by monetary equivalent, the amount constitutes a value credit and must be revalued to the date of judgment with ISTAT indices, with compensatory interest from the date of claim and statutory interest thereafter.
